industry: Churches, faith communities, and community centers (invite mailers, holiday services, VBS/kids, small groups, outreach events)
words_and_claims_to_avoid: Miracle/healing/attendance 'results' presented as typical outcomes ('we healed X people', 'explosive growth guaranteed') without truthful substantiation—usually avoid entirely on acquisition mailers
Government look-alike framing ('official community survey', faux census, fake invoice for 'tithe due') — 39 USC 3001
Deceptive urgency ('last chance for salvation this Sunday only') that implies a false scarcity of grace or a fake deadline
Political candidate endorsements or campaign fundraising on 501(c)(3) church mail (IRS ban on political campaign intervention)
Prize drawings / tablet giveaways without contest rules and no-purchase-necessary where chance + consideration apply (GOLD-churches-community-015/018 patterns)
Implying kids programs are licensed childcare if they are not; overstating background-check practices
'All are welcome' while listing exclusions in microtype that contradict the headline (truth-in-advertising)
compliance_notes: 39 USC 3001: nonmailable matter includes solicitations that look like government documents, fake bills/invoices, and certain sweepstakes without required disclosures. Church invites must look like church invites—not official surveys or invoices.
FTC Act s.5 still reaches deceptive commercial practices; if promoting paid tickets, camps with fees, or merchandise, keep claims truthful.

IRS: 501(c)(3) churches may not intervene in political campaigns for/against candidates (IRS Pub 1828 / IRS guidance). Nonpartisan voter education has limits; candidate fundraising is forbidden. Ordinary worship/event invites are fine.
Fundraising honesty: if asking for donations by mail, identify the organization and purpose; follow state charitable solicitation registration where applicable.
Children's images require parent/guardian consent; youth events should avoid collecting under-13 data online without COPPA-compliant parental consent.
16 CFR 251: 'FREE brunch/VBS/event' must not hide required purchases or donations as conditions in microtype.
Respectful tone is a brand choice; fear/hope/belonging are all allowed when truthful—do not invent afterlife threats as 'research-backed conversion tactics.'
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic and respectful: belonging, hope, peace, joy, even sober urgency are fine when truthful; no fabricated miracles.
Every angle and combo includes sell_the_outcome_line (experience of community/peace/family joy—not doctrinal features alone).
Never invent revival statistics or healing rates.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Prize/gift-card/tablet giveaways on outreach cards (GOLD-churches-community-015/018) vs mail sweepstakes/disclosure rules
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins: if chance + consideration, follow 39 USC 3001(k) and publish rules; prefer free hospitality without a lottery.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Hard fear/urgency salvation framing vs respectful brand preference
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Not a legal ban: emotion-agnostic per Patrick—allowed if truthful and non-deceptive; default creative is belonging/hope unless the client chooses otherwise. Fabricated miracle stats remain forbidden.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Political 'faith voter' mail vs IRS 501(c)(3) campaign intervention ban
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: no candidate endorsements or campaign fundraising on church acquisition mailers.
